clue.text: Support and help for action in court

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
to lend a hand is to help

explanation.surface: Someone seeks backing and assistance to bring a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a stroke played in tennis, a game played on a court, so it is an action there.

clue.text: Incidental actions of actor's company

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stage ..., the small actions an actor performs
second meaning: a firm or commercial enterprise

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe's bits of stage action are described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a theatre company, but it is a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre uses the word for incidental stage action, and commerce uses it for a firm or enterprise.

clue.text: Manoeuvre it on with crane?

indicators.note: to manoeuvre things is to move them about into new positions

explanation.surface: A dockside instruction to swing a load aboard by crane.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of loading a shipping box by crane.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping containers are large boxes swung on and off vessels by dockside cranes.

clue.text: Elevate one of the Romans in legion

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits within it

parts.note: a host is a great number, a legion

explanation.surface: A single Roman soldier is lifted up within his legion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' suggests a Roman army unit, but it means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise or lift it up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Saintly characters are rarely disposed to behave thus

definitions.text: Saintly characters are rarely disposed to behave thus

indicators.note: things disposed are set out or arranged in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Holy people seldom act in a mean way.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Saintly' rearranged give the opposite of saintliness; the whole clue doubles as the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are seldom spiteful, so the way they rarely act is in a mean, unkind manner.

clue.text: Boss  preceding one round workshop

indicators.note: preceding means going in front, so the first piece leads the rest

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: The boss walks ahead of someone on a tour of the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as an employer, but here it is an ornamental knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's working room is a studio, a place where things are made.

clue.text: One blows note in jazz orchestra section

explanation.surface: A wind player sounds a note in a section of a jazz band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One blows' sounds like a player but is something that blows across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are steady tropical winds, so each is something that blows.

clue.text: Abandon in the Channel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dump or discard
second meaning: airmen's slang for the English Channel

explanation.surface: A pilot leaves the aircraft over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF slang called the sea 'the drink' and the English Channel 'the Ditch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means drop or get rid of, and wartime flyers' slang named the Channel with the same noun.

clue.text: Variety of crocus crops up

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take another shape

explanation.surface: A new type of spring bulb appears in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' and 'crops' keep up the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurs happens or turns up, matching the phrasal verb in tense and person.

clue.text: Properly speaking, a ceremonial observance

indicators.note: speaking means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial observance

explanation.surface: Someone, choosing words carefully, describes a formal ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something aright means doing it correctly, an old-fashioned adverb meaning in the right way.

clue.text: Mount in excellent shape after fall

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it, so the clue's first piece goes last

parts.note: the Fall was the first sin, so to fall is to sin
A1 means excellent; written in letter shape the 1 becomes I

explanation.surface: A climber is in fine form after taking a tumble on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping-register mark for first class; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the Egyptian peak where Moses received the Commandments, so it is named as a mount.

clue.text: Scorning South when in Northern region

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: the polar region in the far north
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A Northerner sneers at the South while at home in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sarcastic means mocking someone with scornful irony, so the adjective matches the participle used as a describing word.

clue.text: Making electrically safe after new dangerous incident

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it, so the clue's first piece goes last

parts.note: connecting a circuit to the ground keeps it safe

explanation.surface: An electrician makes a circuit safe after a fresh accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the abbreviation for new first.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, an occasion where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Novel set in royal town

indicators.note: something set in a frame is placed inside it

explanation.surface: A book takes place in a town with royal connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the book 'She'. ESHER is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, England, so it is a straightforward example of a town.

clue.text: Novelist and child, the epitome of happiness

explanation.surface: A writer and a youngster are pictured as perfectly contented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As happy as a sandboy' is a British idiom for being carefree and cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'happy as a sandboy' makes this figure the standard proverbial type of a contented person.

clue.text: Authoritative book's a hit in parts of US

parts.note: a bible is any authoritative reference book; the 's is read as is
a belt is a hard blow

explanation.surface: A definitive book is a bestseller in some American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hit' suggests a success, but it is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible Belt is the swathe of southern American states known for evangelical Protestantism.

clue.text: Tax is about one pound for a novel

indicators.note: being about something means going around it on all sides

parts.note: to tax someone is to try their patience
abbreviation of the Latin libra, a pound weight

explanation.surface: A levy of about a pound is charged on each book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy but is the verb meaning to strain or test.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is George du Maurier's 1894 novel about the singer controlled by Svengali.

clue.text: Fish boy caught finally, like a splendid ray?

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word

explanation.surface: A boy lands a fish and marvels at a fine ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' suggests a fish alongside the brill, but it is a beam of light, and a dazzling one is this.
explanation.definitionFit: A splendid beam of light is dazzlingly bright, and the question mark flags that ray means light, not fish.

clue.text: Playful bit of banter it's hard to follow

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

explanation.surface: Light teasing that is difficult to keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to follow' reads as difficult to understand, but splits into hard plus a placing instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish describes lively, frisky or flighty behaviour, close to playful in sense.

clue.text: Plant is attached to runner, possibly

parts.note: an Arab is a horse, which may be a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A climbing plant clings to a bean runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests a runner bean or stem, but it is a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabis, also called rock cress, is a low flowering garden plant grown in rockeries.

clue.text: Nominal hero mixed drinks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Tristram ..., title hero of Sterne's novel
second meaning: beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink

explanation.surface: A hero in name only is mixing cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristram is the title character of Sterne's novel, yet he is barely born by its end, so he is a hero in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterne's title character barely appears, and the pub drink is beer combined with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Dickens in Marshalsea, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dickens is an old name for the devil
second meaning: the Marshalsea was a historic London debtors' prison, and nick is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens is pictured in the prison where his father was held for debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens wrote about the Marshalsea in Little Dorrit, but here 'Dickens' is the devil, as in 'what the dickens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a nickname for Satan, and taken literally it describes a former jail.

clue.text: Train wandering in circles in area around London

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits within it

parts.note: two circles are two Os, one at each end

indicators.note: something wandering strays from its set path and order

explanation.surface: A commuter train circles aimlessly in the suburbs around London.
explanation.walkthrough: London here is the city in Canada, not England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian province of Ontario contains the city of London, so it is a region surrounding that London.

clue.text: End protest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aim or purpose

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a call to stop a demonstration; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a goal or purpose, and as a verb it means raise an objection.

clue.text: Wash black articles

parts.note: the two articles a and the

explanation.surface: Dark items of clothing are put through the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests garments, but it means the grammatical words a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash oneself or something in water, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Aesthetic judgment society's required in gallery

indicators.note: something needed in a place has to go inside it

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
abbreviation of society; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A cultured eye is what the art world expects in a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the faculty of discerning beauty and quality, the critical sense in matters of style.

clue.text: George and I involved in car scheme

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it

explanation.surface: George and the speaker are mixed up in a dodgy motor deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is pilots' slang for the automatic pilot on an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight control George, so the name is a slang equivalent.

clue.text: Quiet and noble girl, a paragon

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A demure, high-born young woman is held up as a model of virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings follow the wordplay: Pearl is a girl's name, and a pearl is something prized and exemplary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a female first name, and a pearl is also a finest example of something, a model.

clue.text: Sweetheart as affectionate as a TV character

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its very centre

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its central letter

explanation.surface: A lover is as warm-hearted as someone seen on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' must be split into sweet and heart. EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Any figure in the BBC soap EastEnders is an EastEnder, so a television character fits.

clue.text: Dramatist's piece that's highly appreciated by players

indicators.note: a piece of something is a portion cut from within it

parts.note: letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: An actor praises a playwright's work that the cast love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests actors, but it means violinists.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati violins, made by a Cremona family of luthiers, are prized instruments treasured by string musicians.

clue.text: City's right half, outside left, score

indicators.note: one part standing outside another wraps around it
the right half of a word is its second half

explanation.surface: A football report: City's right half and outside left score.
explanation.walkthrough: Right half and outside left look like old football positions, but they direct the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, so the number and the old counting word are equal.

clue.text: Fastening device on cooking-vessel for tribal feast

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
a latch fastens a door or gate

explanation.surface: A lid clip on a cooking pot is used for a communal meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the latch after the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A potlatch is a ceremonial gift-giving gathering among Pacific Northwest peoples, a festive tribal celebration.
